stem: Mild damage is found on 2 plants, then 7, then 15 across three comparable scouting rounds. What is the most important evidence?
choices: Use the first count as the baseline and ignore later increases unless severity also rises.
Treat mild severity as evidence that escalation is unnecessary even when more plants are becoming affected.
Name one specific pest because a steadily rising count confirms a single cause.
Recognize the increasing incidence trend as important evidence and escalate according to procedure even if severity on individual plants remains modest.
rationale: An increase from 2 to 7 to 15 affected plants across comparable rounds shows spread in incidence. Severity can remain mild while the affected scope is expanding, so the trend may still justify escalation. The pattern does not by itself identify one pest, but it is operationally significant.
